idiom_name: methods on a named type inside the concept's package (exported vs unexported API)
implementation_notes: Go replaces the class with two coupled choices: behaviour is attached to a named type through its method set, and the package is the visibility boundary - exported names are the concept's API, unexported ones are internals. Because a method can only be declared in the same package as its receiver type, the package (not the file) is the contour, and domain-named packages are what make the boundary and the ubiquitous language line up.
pitfalls: A receiver type and its methods must share one package, so there are no extension methods: extending another package's concept means wrapping it or writing free functions in the client's package, either of which moves behaviour away from the type.
Embedding promotes the embedded type's methods into the outer method set, so two embedded concepts blur the outer contour and its exported API.
Mixing pointer and value receivers splits the method set (value instances in interfaces lose pointer-receiver methods), which changes what the concept exposes.
